report.summary: Analyzed chunk 5 of daedalus/council/session.py: council execution loop, budget round, floor refusal, turn refs, and participant records. Claims checked: floor_check prevents any vendor call; budget rounds record all participants; _chained reads from chain; _turn_ref extracts fields; _first_offending_path returns first path; _unavailable_turn produces unavailable turn; _append_budget_round records round. All claims kept.
risks: _first_offending_path | low | The function _first_offending_path checks only the path channel, not the file content channel. A file whose name is safe but content contains a secret floor pattern would be missed. To settle, confirm that file content is also checked elsewhere, or that the design intends only path-based checks for the refusal receipt.

claims.text: A hit refuses the whole council -- there is no redact-and-send -- and NO VENDOR IS CALLED.
claims.why: The code checks floor_refusal before any vendor dispatch; if refusal is not None, it immediately constructs floor refusal turns and sets ended='floor_refusal', without calling any vendor.

claims.text: a blown wall clock is NOT handled here: the next iteration's top-of-round check records a budget_exhausted turn per participant first. Breaking early would shorten the council silently.
claims.why: The loop does not break on wall clock; the next iteration's top check (remaining <= 0) calls _append_budget_round which records budget turns for all participants, then breaks.

claims.text: A blown budget is a RECORDED round, not a shortened one.
claims.why: The function appends a round with budget turns for all seated participants and updates outcomes, ensuring the round is recorded.

claims.text: Read this round's turns back FROM THE CHAIN. Round 2 prompts are built from these, not from the in-memory replies: a turn the secret floor refused is a receipt on disk, and re-feeding the raw reply would smuggle the refused bytes into another vendor's prompt.
claims.why: The function loads turns from the chain via load_transcript, filtering by record type and round number, ensuring only recorded turns are used.

claims.text: The first path whose PATH channel fires, for the refusal receipt.
claims.why: The function iterates over evidence.paths and evidence.files, returns the first path where secret_floor_rule(path, '') returns True, or empty string.

claims.text: Hung or crashed: recorded as a turn, never as an absence.
claims.why: When reply is None, _unavailable_turn is called and appended to batch, recording a turn with status 'unavailable'.

claims.text: Nobody had a voice this round; another round would prompt on an empty transcript and pretend to be a deliberation.
claims.why: After processing a round, if spoke_any is False, the loop breaks with ended='no_voice', preventing further rounds.

claims.text: Charge the token ceiling BEFORE dispatch, from the assembled prompt. Reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.why: The code counts tokens for body and evidence before dispatching, and increments tokens_charged per job; if over budget, the adapter is added to over_budget list.

claims.text: A trusted lane disables the egress allow-list and reports nothing withheld.
claims.why: The comment is part of a ValueError message; the actual behavior of trusted lanes is not defined in this chunk (likely defined elsewhere).

observations.what: The function _first_offending_path checks only the path channel, not the file content channel. A file whose name is safe but content contains a secret floor pattern would be missed.
In _chained, the function filters by record type 'turn' and round number, but does not sort or order the results. The order may depend on load_transcript.
The variable 'prior' is built from chained records that have non-empty content; this includes only turns that actually spoke. This is used as prior context for the next round.
